reports.afni_fit_note: Best used as the "attack/fuzz" half of a red-team pipeline feeding findings into a separate runtime guardrail layer (e.g. Presidio/Guardrails/NeMo-style detectors) for AFNI's unified toolkit; its own PII/refusal/sandbox-escape detectors are simple regex heuristics that should not be relied on as the production guardrail.
reports.core_functionality: Agentic Security (repo folder agentic_security-main, package `agentic_security`) is a FastAPI/uvicorn web app + CLI (entry point agentic_security.__main__:main, app defined in agentic_security/app.py and core/app.py) that fuzzes a target LLM/agent HTTP endpoint with adversarial prompts and scores whether the target "fell for" the attack. The core loop lives in probe_actor/fuzzer.py: scan_router() dispatches to perform_single_shot_scan() (send individual prompts from selected datasets) or perform_many_shot_scan() (inject probe prompts into long multi-turn contexts to test many-shot-jailbreak/context-window attacks). Prompts are pulled by probe_data/data.py's prepare_prompts(), which hydrates ~25 hard-coded HuggingFace jailbreak/prompt-injection datasets (DAN_jailbreak, deepset/prompt-injections, JailbreakBench, JailbreakHub, JailBreakV-28K, AdvBench via EasyJailbreak, ChatGPT-Jailbreak-Prompts, etc.), local/uploaded CSVs, Google-Sheets CSV exports, and dynamically-generated "modules" (Steganography obfuscation, llm-adaptive-attacks template prompts, Garak probe integration, RL-optimized prompt selection, InspectAI eval integration, an "AgenticBackend"/fine_tuned module and RL module that call out to an external hosted service https://mcp.metaheuristic.co with a hard-coded fallback bearer token). Multimodal support renders each text prompt into a matplotlib-generated image (probe_data/image_generator.py, typographic-attack style) or gTTS-generated audio (audio_generator.py) and posts it as base64 to vision/audio endpoints. attack_rules/ lets teams author custom AttackRule YAML files (name/type/prompt/severity/pass_conditions/fail_conditions) loaded by RuleLoader and turned into a ProbeDataset. After each prompt, the response is judged by a pluggable "detector" pipeline (refusal_classifier/): a phrase-list DefaultRefusalClassifier (~28 hard-coded refusal phrases like "I'm sorry", "As an AI", "I cannot"), a pre-trained scikit-learn One-Class-SVM RefusalClassifier (TF-IDF vectorizer + StandardScaler + OneClassSVM, shipped as joblib files trained on GPT-4/ChatGPT/Claude refusal transcripts), an optional PIIDetector (regex, deterministic), an optional SandboxEscapeDetector (regex, deterministic), an optional LLMRefusalClassifier that calls out to OpenAI/Anthropic as an LLM-judge ("promptmap"-style controller prompt), and a HybridRefusalClassifier that does weighted voting across all of them with a confidence score. A DetectorRegistry lets ops enable/disable/add detectors via an `agesec.toml` `[detectors]` config section without editing code. Bayesian optimization (scikit-optimize Optimizer over a 1-D failure-rate objective) is used to early-stop scanning a dataset module once observed failure rate exceeds a threshold, and a token/cost budget (calculate_cost) bounds total spend. Results stream back as JSON (ScanResult) over SSE/StreamingResponse for the bundled web UI, and failing/complete logs are exported to CSV (failures.csv, full_scan_log.csv). A CI mode (`agentic_security init` / `agentic_security` CLI) generates an agesec.toml config with threshold gating for pipeline use.

granular_aspects.description: DefaultRefusalClassifier in probe_actor/refusal.py checks ~28 hard-coded substrings (e.g. "I'm sorry", "As an AI", "I cannot", "is illegal and unethical") to flag that the target model refused the adversarial prompt.

refusal_classifier/model.py RefusalClassifier: TF-IDF vectorizer + StandardScaler + OneClassSVM trained on GPT-4/ChatGPT/Claude refusal transcripts, shipped as pre-trained joblib artifacts, used to catch refusals the phrase list misses.

refusal_classifier/llm_classifier.py LLMRefusalClassifier sends the target's response plus pass/fail condition lists to a controller LLM (OpenAI gpt-4o-mini or Anthropic claude-3-haiku) that returns a single-word pass/fail verdict on whether the jailbreak succeeded.
hybrid_classifier.py HybridRefusalClassifier combines marker/ML/LLM detector votes with configurable weights and threshold, producing an is_refusal decision plus a 0-1 confidence score.
PIIDetector regex pattern flags email addresses in model responses.
PIIDetector regex pattern (excluding invalid 000/666/9xx area codes) flags US Social Security Numbers.
PIIDetector regex flags US-style phone numbers in responses.
PIIDetector regex flags PEM-format private key headers (RSA/DSA/EC/OPENSSH/PGP) leaking in output.

granular_aspects.description: PIIDetector finds 13-19 digit candidate sequences and validates them with the Luhn checksum algorithm to reduce false positives before flagging as a credit-card leak.

SandboxEscapeDetector regexes flag capability probing (capsh/getpcaps/CapEff), mount/docker.sock inspection, kernel-exploit reconnaissance (uname -a, searchsploit, CVE IDs, dirtycow/dirtypipe), and Kubernetes service-account/API probing in model output.

perform_many_shot_scan() repeatedly injects random probe prompts from MSJ datasets into a growing context until a max context length is hit, then injects the real attack prompt, testing susceptibility to many-shot jailbreaking.

stenography_fn.py implements rot13, rot5, base64, mirror-words, random-case, word-scramble, noise-character insertion, ascii-substitution, vowel-removal, zigzag-case, Caesar cipher, substitution cipher, and Vigenere cipher transforms applied to jailbreak prompts to test whether obfuscation bypasses safety filters.

probe_data/modules/adaptive_attacks.py ports the tml-epfl llm-adaptive-attacks universal manual prompt templates (refined_best, icl_one_shot, claude, refined_best_simplified) that wrap a harmful goal in role-play/rule-following scaffolding designed to bypass alignment.

probe_data/modules/rl_model.py implements a local Q-learning prompt selector (with exploration decay) and a CloudRLPromptSelector that calls a hosted API to pick the next adversarial prompt based on whether prior prompts bypassed the guard, adapting the attack strategy over the scan.

image_generator.py renders attack text into an image (4 visual themes) and audio_generator.py synthesizes attack text as speech via gTTS, then base64-encodes and posts them to vision/audio LLM endpoints to test cross-modal safety bypass.

attack_rules/loader.py + models.py let a team define named, severity-tagged (low/medium/high) attack rules with explicit pass/fail conditions in YAML files, validated for required fields and loaded into scan datasets — giving an auditable, versionable rule set.

granular_aspects.description: scan_module() in fuzzer.py uses a scikit-optimize Gaussian-Process Optimizer over observed failure rates to decide when a dataset module's failure rate has crossed FAILURE_RATE_THRESHOLD (default 0.5) and stop early, keeping scan cost/time bounded and auditable via ScanResult status messages.

core/security.py SecurityValidator.validate_url blocks non-http(s) schemes, localhost/0.0.0.0, and private 10.x/192.168.x/169.254.x ranges before the app will fetch a user-supplied dataset URL, though it does not cover all RFC1918 ranges (e.g. 172.16-31.x) or DNS-rebinding.
core/security.py sanitize_log_output() regex-redacts api_key/token/password/secret/Bearer values before they are written to logs.

limitations: Its own built-in detectors (refusal phrase list, PII regexes, sandbox-escape regexes) are simple heuristics/regex, not calibrated against a labeled benchmark in the repo — no precision/recall numbers are published for any detector; the ML classifier is a one-class SVM with no reported accuracy either.

Several 'modules' (fine_tuned.py 'AgenticBackend', rl_model.py 'Reinforcement Learning Optimization') silently call out to a third-party hosted service at https://mcp.metaheuristic.co using a hard-coded fallback bearer token embedded in source (AS_TOKEN default) — a real integration risk (data exfiltration / vendor dependency) that a security team must explicitly disable/override.

Garak and Inspect AI integrations only work if those packages are separately pip-installed and are invoked via subprocess/shell, adding operational fragility and platform (POSIX shell) assumptions; garak_tool.py only wires up the 'encoding' probe by default (marked TODO for more).

IBM's AI Fairness 360 (Trusted-AI/AIF360) is a Python/R toolkit that computes group- and individual-fairness metrics on datasets and classifiers, scans for biased subgroups (MDSS, FACTS), and ships ~15 bias-mitigation algorithms (pre/in/post-processing) plus human-readable explainers.
reports.core_functionality: Verified by reading source: the core aif360/metrics/ package (dataset_metric.py, binary_label_dataset_metric.py, classification_metric.py, sample_distortion_metric.py, regression_metric.py, ot_metric.py) implements object-oriented metric classes that wrap an AIF360 StructuredDataset/BinaryLabelDataset plus privileged/unprivileged group definitions and expose dozens of concrete fairness computations (confusion-matrix-derived rates, disparate impact, statistical parity, entropy indices, etc.). aif360/detectors/mdss_detector.py implements bias_scan(), a wrapper around aif360/detectors/mdss/MDSS.py (a Multi-Dimensional Subset Scan optimizer) parameterized by pluggable likelihood-ratio scoring functions in aif360/detectors/mdss/ScoringFunctions/ (Bernoulli.py, BerkJones.py, Gaussian.py, Poisson.py) to find the highest-scoring biased subgroup of records (over/under-predicted) without exhaustively enumerating subgroups. aif360/sklearn/detectors/facts/ implements the FACTS framework (misc.py, optimization.py, predicate.py, frequent_itemsets.py, rule_filters.py, formatting.py) which mines frequent-itemset subgroup predicates and computes counterfactual "recourse cost" disparities between subgroups for a trained sklearn-style classifier, exposed via FACTS_bias_scan(). aif360/sklearn/metrics/metrics.py re-exposes ~35 of these as plain scikit-learn-style scoring functions (disparate_impact_ratio, average_odds_difference, generalized_entropy_error, mdss_bias_score, consistency_score, etc.) usable directly with sklearn Pipelines/GridSearchCV. aif360/algorithms/{preprocessing,inprocessing,postprocessing}/ implement ~15 published bias-mitigation algorithms as Transformer subclasses (fit/transform pattern) operating on the dataset/classifier: Reweighing, Disparate Impact Remover, Learning Fair Representations (LFR, PyTorch), Optimized Preprocessing (CVXPY), Adversarial Debiasing (TensorFlow v1), Prejudice Remover, Meta Fair Classifier, GerryFair (rich subgroup fairness), Exponentiated Gradient/Grid Search Reduction (via fairlearn), Calibrated Equalized-Odds Postprocessing, Equalized Odds Postprocessing, Reject Option Classification, and Deterministic Reranking. aif360/explainers/metric_text_explainer.py and metric_json_explainer.py wrap any Metric object and turn each numeric metric into a plain-English or JSON explanation string. Confirmed usage via tests/test_demo_mdss_classifier_metric.py (which runs examples/demo_mdss_classifier_metric.ipynb through nbconvert) and other test_demo_*.py files that execute the corresponding example notebooks end-to-end as the test suite.
key_features: BinaryLabelDatasetMetric / ClassificationMetric classes exposing 50+ group-fairness metrics (disparate impact, statistical parity difference, average odds difference, equal opportunity difference, TPR/FPR/FNR/TNR and their differences/ratios, generalized entropy index, Theil index, differential fairness & bias amplification)
MDSS bias_scan() detector: fast subgroup discovery using Bernoulli/Gaussian/Poisson/BerkJones scoring functions to flag the subset of records most biased vs. model expectations
FACTS bias scan: counterfactual-recourse-based subgroup fairness detector for trained classifiers, using frequent-itemset rule mining

~15 bias-mitigation algorithms spanning pre-processing (Reweighing, Disparate Impact Remover, LFR, Optimized Preprocessing), in-processing (Adversarial Debiasing, Prejudice Remover, Meta Fair Classifier, GerryFair, Exponentiated-Gradient/Grid-Search Reduction), and post-processing (Equalized Odds, Calibrated Equalized Odds, Reject Option Classification, Deterministic Reranking)
scikit-learn-compatible metrics API (aif360.sklearn.metrics) usable as scorers in sklearn pipelines/GridSearchCV without AIF360's custom Dataset objects
Sample-distortion metrics (Euclidean/Manhattan/Mahalanobis distance based) to quantify how much a mitigation algorithm changed the data
Optimal-transport (Wasserstein) fairness metric (ot_metric.py) via the POT library
Human-readable and JSON explainers that auto-generate plain-English descriptions of any computed metric value
R package mirror (aif360-r) and standard benchmark dataset loaders (Adult, COMPAS, German Credit, Bank, MEPS, etc.) in aif360/datasets

granular_aspects.aspect: Generalized entropy index / Theil index / coefficient of variation
granular_aspects.description: Individual-fairness inequality metrics (Speicher et al. 2018) computed within- and between-group on benefit vectors.
Smoothed empirical differential fairness metric and bias-amplification score (Foulds et al. 2018) across all subgroup combinations, not just two groups.
kNN-based measure of whether similar individuals receive similar predictions (dataset_metric consistency()).
rich_subgroup() metric plus GerryFairClassifier detect/mitigate fairness violations across exponentially many overlapping subgroups defined by linear/polynomial functions of features.
Multi-Dimensional Subset Scan detector that efficiently searches for the highest-scoring biased subgroup of records (over- or under-predicted) instead of checking predefined groups.
Mines frequent-itemset subgroup predicates and compares counterfactual 'cost of recourse' to flag which subgroups face systematically harder paths to a favorable outcome.
Quantifies how much a preprocessing/mitigation transform altered the original data, per-group and per-instance.
ot_metric.py computes optimal-transport distance between group outcome distributions as an alternative fairness measure.
MetricTextExplainer/MetricJSONExplainer auto-generate plain-language or structured explanations for any computed fairness metric value.
Reweights training instances per (group,label) combo to remove label/attribute correlation before training.

granular_aspects.aspect: Disparate Impact Remover / Optimized Preprocessing / LFR
granular_aspects.description: Transform feature distributions (via repair, convex optimization, or learned fair latent representations) to reduce group disparity in the data itself.

granular_aspects.aspect: Adversarial Debiasing / Prejudice Remover / Meta Fair Classifier / Exponentiated Gradient & Grid Search Reduction
granular_aspects.description: In-processing algorithms that constrain or adversarially regularize model training to reduce disparate outcomes while fitting.

granular_aspects.aspect: Equalized Odds / Calibrated Equalized Odds Postprocessing / Reject Option Classification / Deterministic Reranking
granular_aspects.description: Post-hoc adjustment of model scores/decisions (threshold shifting, calibrated randomization, reranking) to satisfy equalized-odds or statistical-parity constraints after training.

limitations: Purely a fairness/bias toolkit for structured tabular ML models (classification/regression on protected attributes) - it has no notion of LLM prompts, jailbreaks, PII entities, secrets, or content-safety categories, so it cannot serve as a generic GenAI guardrail out of the box.

Several algorithms carry heavy/legacy optional dependencies that must be installed as extras and can be brittle: TensorFlow 1.x (compat.v1) for AdversarialDebiasing, CVXPY (+ platform build tools) for OptimPreproc, PyTorch for LFR, BlackBoxAuditing for DisparateImpactRemover, rpy2 for FairAdapt (requires R), fairlearn for the Reduction algorithms.

Fairness metrics require the user to pre-define 'privileged'/'unprivileged' groups and a favorable label; results (and even which metric is 'correct') are use-case and value-judgment dependent - the maintainers explicitly publish separate guidance material because misuse/misinterpretation is common.

MDSS and FACTS detectors operate on data/predictions the user supplies (dataframes, a fitted sklearn classifier) - there's no runtime request/response interception; integrating into a live guardrail pipeline requires custom orchestration code.

setup.py classifies the package as 'Development Status: 3 - Alpha' and pins scikit-learn to <1.6, signalling ongoing compatibility churn; some algorithm subfolders (celisMeta, gerryfair, kamfadm-2012ecmlpkdd, lfr_helpers) are vendored research code with their own README/paper-specific caveats.
No hallucination/groundedness, security, or privacy detectors of any kind are present in this repo - its guardrail relevance to AFNI's GenAI risk categories is limited to the Fairness & Bias tenet.
prerequisites: Python 3.10-3.13 (or R via aif360-r/CRAN)
numpy, scipy, pandas, scikit-learn (<1.6), matplotlib (core, always required)

Optional heavy extras depending on algorithm used: tensorflow>=1.13 (AdversarialDebiasing), cvxpy (OptimPreproc), torch (LFR), BlackBoxAuditing (DisparateImpactRemover), fairlearn (Reductions), rpy2/R (FairAdapt), skorch+inFairness, POT (optimal transport), mlxtend/colorama (FACTS)
No GPU or paid/hosted API required for any component - everything runs locally/offline on CPU (TensorFlow/PyTorch pieces can optionally use GPU but don't require it)
A labeled tabular dataset with defined protected attribute(s) and favorable/unfavorable label to compute any metric
reports.integration_effort_reason: Core metrics/detectors (metrics/, detectors/, sklearn/metrics, sklearn/detectors) are pure Python + numpy/pandas/scikit-learn and can be called directly from a Flask/FastAPI backend with modest glue code (wrap a dataframe + predictions into a BinaryLabelDataset or call the sklearn-style functions/bias_scan/FACTS_bias_scan) - this part is Low effort. Effort rises to Medium/High if the specific mitigation algorithm needed depends on TensorFlow 1.x, CVXPY, PyTorch, R/rpy2, or fairlearn, each adding its own install/version friction, and because there is no built-in HTTP service, request middleware, or streaming interface - a team must build its own API layer, data adapters (raw features -> AIF360 Dataset objects), and decide which of the many metrics/algorithms map to their governance requirements.
reports.reliability_notes: Metrics themselves are deterministic, well-established published formulas (many with direct academic citations inline in docstrings, e.g. Speicher et al. 2018 entropy index, Foulds et al. 2018 differential fairness, Kearns et al. 2018 rich subgroup fairness, Kavouras et al. 2023 FACTS) so numerical reliability for a given definition is high and auditable from the code. The MDSS/FACTS detectors are heuristic subset-search optimizers (random-restart local search, frequent-itemset mining) - they are not guaranteed to find the globally worst subgroup and their output depends on tunable parameters (num_iters, penalty, freq_itemset_min_supp). The project has a CI badge, ReadTheDocs, a large tests/ suite that runs every example notebook end-to-end (test_demo_*.py via nbconvert) plus dedicated unit tests (test_classification_metric.py, test_differential_fairness.py, test_ot_metric.py, etc.), and is maintained under the Linux-Foundation-adjacent Trusted-AI GitHub org with an active MAINTAINERS.md and CONTRIBUTING.rst - signals of a moderately mature, still-active research-grade project (setup.py itself self-labels 'Development Status: 3 - Alpha').
reports.afni_fit_note: Slots in as the Fairness & Bias measurement/mitigation layer of a unified AFNI toolkit - feed it tabular model inputs/outputs (or wrap traditional-ML decision endpoints) to compute standardized bias metrics and run MDSS/FACTS subgroup scans in batch/offline evaluation jobs; it does not cover LLM-specific risks (PII, jailbreaks, hallucination, content safety) so must be paired with other repos in the 23-repo set for those tenets.

reports.one_line_summary: An open-source Python testing/validation framework (Checks + Suites architecture) that runs dozens of built-in statistical and model-based checks against tabular, NLP/LLM-text, and computer-vision data/models to catch data integrity issues, train/test drift, and performance/fairness problems before and after deployment.
reports.core_functionality: The core package (deepchecks/core/checks.py, condition.py, check_result.py, suite.py) defines an abstract BaseCheck hierarchy (SingleDatasetBaseCheck, TrainTestBaseCheck, ModelOnlyBaseCheck) plus a Condition/ConditionResult system: each Check's run() returns a CheckResult (a value + optional Plotly display), and user-added Conditions turn that value into a PASS/FAIL/WARN/ERROR verdict that a Suite aggregates and that CI pipelines can gate on (junit/json serializers under core/serialization confirm CI intent). Three parallel domain packages (deepchecks/tabular, deepchecks/nlp, deepchecks/vision) each ship checks/{data_integrity,train_test_validation,model_evaluation} subpackages with the same architecture applied to a Dataset/TextData/VisionData object. I opened deepchecks/nlp/checks/data_integrity/unknown_tokens.py (tokenizes samples with a HuggingFace tokenizer, e.g. bert-base-uncased, and flags words that hash to the [UNK] token, with a pie-chart display and an add_condition_ratio_of_unknown_words_less_or_equal condition) and confirmed it against its test file tests/nlp/checks/data_integrity/unknown_tokens_test.py, which exercises fast vs. slow tokenizers, singleton grouping, and illegal-tokenizer validation. deepchecks/nlp/utils/text_properties.py implements the actual per-text scoring functions (regex/NLTK/TextBlob-based length, punctuation, sentiment, readability, syllables, URL/email counts; transformer-pipeline-based Toxicity/Fluency/Formality; fastText-based Language ID) that feed the property-based checks (TextPropertyOutliers, PropertyDrift, PropertyLabelCorrelation, UnderAnnotatedPropertySegments). deepchecks/utils/distribution/drift.py implements the shared drift-scoring engine (PSI, Cramer's V, Wasserstein/Earth-Mover's distance, Kolmogorov-Smirnov) used by every *Drift check across all three domains. deepchecks/tabular/checks/data_integrity/outlier_sample_detection.py implements outlier detection via the LoOP algorithm (PyNomaly) over a Gower distance matrix. deepchecks/tabular/checks/model_evaluation/performance_bias.py and deepchecks/utils/abstracts/weak_segment_abstract.py implement fairness/robustness diagnostics: PerformanceBias measures per-subgroup performance deltas against a 'protected feature', and WeakSegmentsPerformance trains a shallow DecisionTreeRegressor/GridSearchCV over feature space to auto-discover underperforming data segments. deepchecks/nlp/suites/default_suites.py shows how ~9-10 checks are wired into a single 'Data Integrity Suite' with pre-attached conditions, matching what pip-installed users actually run.
key_features: Check/Condition/Suite framework: every check returns a typed CheckResult; conditions convert results into PASS/FAIL verdicts a CI pipeline (junit/json output serializers) can gate on
Three parallel domains -- deepchecks.tabular, deepchecks.nlp, deepchecks.vision -- each with data_integrity, train_test_validation, and model_evaluation check families

Shared statistical drift engine (PSI, Cramer's V, Wasserstein distance, Kolmogorov-Smirnov) reused across FeatureDrift, LabelDrift, PredictionDrift, PropertyDrift, MultivariateDrift/WholeDatasetDrift, ImagePropertyDrift, TextEmbeddingsDrift

NLP text-property engine (deepchecks/nlp/utils/text_properties.py) computing 15+ default and 24 total per-text properties, including model-based Toxicity/Fluency/Formality scores via HuggingFace transformer pipelines (with ONNX-accelerated variants) and fastText language identification
Vision image-property engine (aspect ratio, area, brightness, RMS contrast, mean R/G/B relative intensity) feeding image/label property outlier and drift checks
LoOP + Gower-distance multivariate outlier detection for tabular data (OutlierSampleDetection)

Fairness/robustness diagnostics: PerformanceBias (subgroup performance gap vs. a protected feature, optionally stratified by a control feature) and WeakSegmentsPerformance / UnderAnnotatedPropertySegments (decision-tree-based automatic discovery of underperforming or under-labeled data segments), implemented per-domain (tabular/nlp/vision)
Rich HTML/Plotly/Jupyter/Wandb/JUnit result serialization for CI & Testing Management integration

Companion open-source 'Deepchecks Monitoring' product (separate repo) for production drift/quality tracking, plus benchmarks/ dir (asv-based) for performance regression tracking of the checks themselves

granular_aspects.description: Per-text-sample toxicity score (0-1) computed via the SkolkovoInstitute/roberta_toxicity_classifier transformer model (ONNX variant available), calibrated with a pickled probability calibrator; fed into TextPropertyOutliers, PropertyDrift, and UnderAnnotated/PropertySegmentsPerformance checks.

Model-based scores of text register (s-nlp/roberta-base-formality-ranker) and fluency (prithivida/parrot_fluency_model) used as data-quality/text-quality signals feeding outlier and drift checks, not safety filters per se.
TextBlob-based polarity and subjectivity scores per text sample, exposed as inspectable dataset-level properties rather than opaque judgments.

fastText language-ID model used both as a standalone property and to gate which 'English-only' properties (sentiment, toxicity, fluency, formality, reading ease, syllable counts) are computed, avoiding spurious low-confidence scores on non-English text.

Simple regex-based counters (unique/non-unique email address and URL counts) in text_properties.py -- a coarse leakage/PII-adjacent signal, not a full PII entity classifier (no SSN/credit-card/phone/name detection).

UnknownTokens check (nlp/checks/data_integrity/unknown_tokens.py) tokenizes text with a HuggingFace tokenizer and flags words mapping to [UNK], surfacing tokenizer/vocabulary mismatches that would degrade a downstream LLM/model's understanding of the data.

granular_aspects.description: utils/distribution/drift.py implements four standard distribution-shift metrics reused by every *Drift check (feature, label, prediction, multivariate/whole-dataset, property, image, embeddings) across tabular/nlp/vision to catch train/production skew that causes silent model degradation.

nlp/checks/train_test_validation/text_embeddings_drift.py + utils/multivariate_embeddings_drift_utils.py compare sentence-embedding distributions (sentence_transformers) between train/test or reference/production text sets to detect semantic drift beyond surface statistics.
Tabular check using the LoOP local-outlier-probability algorithm over a Gower distance matrix (mixed numeric/categorical) to flag anomalous rows likely to be data errors.
Vision checks computing aspect ratio, area, brightness, RMS contrast, and mean R/G/B relative intensity per image, used to detect corrupted images, lighting/quality shifts, or camera/domain drift.

tabular/checks/model_evaluation/performance_bias.py explicitly computes per-subgroup performance differences relative to baseline for a designated 'protected feature' (optionally stratified by a control feature) -- a direct subgroup-fairness diagnostic.

Shared WeakSegmentAbstract trains a shallow decision tree over feature/property space (with GridSearchCV) to auto-discover data segments with disproportionately weak model performance or label-annotation coverage; implemented per-domain (tabular, nlp: Metadata/PropertySegmentsPerformance, vision).
Tabular/NLP integrity checks that detect label imbalance, ID-leakage-via-correlation, and label-conflicting duplicate samples, all of which can encode or mask bias in training data.

core/condition.py + core/checks.py formalize each check's pass/fail threshold as an auditable, named ConditionResult object, and Suite results serialize to JUnit XML / JSON / Wandb for CI gating and audit trails.

It is AGPLv3-licensed, which has copyleft implications for a commercial product embedding it as a library

reports.one_line_summary: An open-source, pytest-style Python framework (by Confident AI) that ships ~50 ready-made LLM-as-judge and NLP-model metrics (hallucination, bias, toxicity, PII leakage, faithfulness, relevancy, tool/agent correctness, etc.) plus academic benchmark harnesses, for unit-testing and CI-gating LLM apps and agents.
reports.core_functionality: DeepEval's `deepeval/metrics` package (52 subfolders) defines a `BaseMetric` interface with sync `measure()`/async `a_measure()` methods. Most metrics (e.g. BiasMetric, ToxicityMetric, PIILeakageMetric, MisuseMetric, RoleViolationMetric, NonAdviceMetric, HallucinationMetric, FaithfulnessMetric, GEval) are LLM-as-judge: they build a prompt from a `Template` class (found in each metric's `templates/` folder, e.g. `generate_verdicts.txt`, `class.txt`, `generate_reason.txt`), send it to a `DeepEvalBaseLLM` (default: OpenAI via `deepeval/models/llms`), parse a structured Pydantic schema (`schema.py` per metric) of per-statement 'verdicts' (yes/no + reason), and compute score = fraction of clean verdicts. A minority of metrics are fully deterministic/library-based with no model call: `PatternMatchMetric` (regex `re.fullmatch`), `ExactMatchMetric`, `ToolPermissionMetric` (allow/deny-list set membership on `ToolCall.name`), and `AgentLoopDetectionMetric` (difflib `SequenceMatcher`/Jaccard similarity across agent steps to catch repetition loops, no LLM). A separate `deepeval/scorer/scorer.py` `Scorer` class provides classic NLP metrics (ROUGE, BLEU, exact/quasi-exact match, BERTScore via `bert_score`) plus optional local-model scorers: `SummaCModels` (SummaCZS faithfulness), `HallucinationModel` (Vectara hallucination model), `DetoxifyModel` (HuggingFace Detoxify, local, GPU-optional) and `UnBiasedModel` (Dbias classifier) for non-LLM-judge bias/toxicity scoring. `deepeval/benchmarks/` implements 17 academic benchmark harnesses (ARC, BBQ, Big-Bench-Hard, BoolQ, DROP, EquityMedQA, GSM8K, HellaSwag, HumanEval, IFEval, LAMBADA, LogiQA, MathQA, MMLU, SQuAD, TruthfulQA, Winogrande) each with a `template.py` prompt-builder and task list. `deepeval/synthesizer` generates synthetic eval datasets; `deepeval/tracing` provides `@observe` decorators for trajectory capture; `deepeval/cli` exposes a `deepeval test run` pytest-plugin CLI and `deepeval login`/`deepeval view` for the optional Confident AI SaaS. Note: the former `red_teaming` module is now a stub — its README says the red-teaming/jailbreak functionality was spun out to a separate sibling project, DeepTeam (github.com/confident-ai/deepteam), so this repo itself does not ship attack/jailbreak techniques.

G-Eval (LLM-as-judge on custom natural-language criteria) and DAG (deterministic decision-graph LLM-judge builder) for fully custom checks
Safety/compliance-flavored metrics: PIILeakageMetric, MisuseMetric (domain-restricted), NonAdviceMetric, RoleViolationMetric, ToolPermissionMetric
Deterministic, model-free metrics: PatternMatchMetric (regex), ExactMatchMetric, ToolPermissionMetric, AgentLoopDetectionMetric (difflib-based loop/stagnation detector)

17 academic benchmark harnesses (MMLU, HellaSwag, DROP, BIG-Bench-Hard, TruthfulQA, HumanEval, GSM8K, ARC, BBQ, BoolQ, IFEval, LAMBADA, LogiQA, MathQA, SQuAD, Winogrande, EquityMedQA) runnable against any custom LLM wrapper

granular_aspects.description: LLM-as-judge (deepeval/metrics/hallucination) checks actual_output against provided context for factual contradictions, using a verdict schema and score = fraction of non-contradicted context items.
Checks whether RAG output is factually grounded in retrieval_context; also has a non-LLM local alternative via Scorer.faithfulness_score using the SummaCZS model (deepeval/models/summac_model.py).
Scorer.hallucination_score loads deepeval/models/hallucination_model.py (Vectara's hallucination-evaluation model) to score prediction vs. source without any LLM call.
Three RAG metrics judging whether retrieved context nodes are ranked well, cover the expected output, and are relevant to the input, each via its own LLM-judge template.
LLM-judge measuring whether actual_output addresses the input; backed by an answer_relevancy_model.py helper.
Multi-turn variants (turn_faithfulness, turn_relevancy, turn_contextual_precision/recall/relevancy) applying the same judge pattern per conversation turn.

LLM-judge (metrics/bias) detects gender/racial/political bias in outputs via generated opinion statements and yes/no bias verdicts; alternative local UnBiasedModel (Dbias classifier, models/unbias_model.py) usable via Scorer for non-LLM bias scoring.

LLM-judge (metrics/toxicity) extracts opinions and judges toxicity per statement; alternative local DetoxifyModel (HuggingFace Detoxify, models/detoxify_model.py) returns toxicity/severe_toxicity/obscene/threat/insult/identity_attack sub-scores via Scorer.neural_toxic_score.
metrics/pii_leakage extracts candidate PII strings from actual_output via LLM, then judges each as a genuine privacy violation or not; score = fraction with no leak.
metrics/misuse takes a required `domain` (e.g. 'medical', 'legal') and uses an LLM judge to flag out-of-scope/unsafe domain-specific misuse in actual_output.
metrics/non_advice LLM-judge flags cases where the model gives disallowed professional advice (templates include generate_advices.txt).
metrics/role_violation checks whether the assistant broke an assigned persona/role via LLM judge given a required `role` string.
Multi-turn LLM-judge verifying the chatbot consistently stays in its assigned role/persona across a conversation.
Fully deterministic, no-LLM metric (metrics/tool_permission/tool_permission.py) enforcing an allow-list/deny-list of tool names against ToolCall objects; score = fraction of authorized calls.

granular_aspects.aspect: Tool Correctness / Argument Correctness / Tool Use Metrics
granular_aspects.description: Check that an agent called the expected tools with expected arguments and used them appropriately (mix of deterministic comparison and LLM-judge).
Deterministic regex full-match checker (metrics/pattern_match/pattern_match.py) — compiles a user-supplied pattern and scores 1.0 only on full match; no model dependency, cheap CI gate.

granular_aspects.aspect: Exact Match / Quasi Exact Match / Quasi Contains
granular_aspects.description: Scorer.exact_match_score / quasi_exact_match_score / quasi_contains_score do plain/normalized string equality/containment checks for deterministic grading.

Deterministic detector (difflib.SequenceMatcher + Jaccard similarity over stop-word-filtered tokens) that flags an agent repeating near-identical reasoning/steps without progress — a reliability/stagnation guardrail, no LLM call.
LLM-judge verifying the conversation stayed within an allowed set of topics.
Multi-turn LLM-judge checking the chatbot doesn't ask for or forget information already provided earlier in the conversation.
Deterministic/schema-based check that actual_output parses into and matches an expected JSON schema.

G-Eval lets teams define arbitrary natural-language grading criteria evaluated by an LLM judge with chain-of-thought scoring steps; DAG builds a deterministic decision graph of LLM-judge nodes for auditable, structured custom checks.
Classic NLP overlap/similarity metrics in deepeval/scorer/scorer.py for summarization/translation-style grading without any LLM call.

granular_aspects.aspect: Academic benchmark harnesses (MMLU, BBQ, TruthfulQA, HellaSwag, GSM8K, HumanEval, DROP, ARC, BoolQ, IFEval, LAMBADA, LogiQA, MathQA, SQuAD, Winogrande, Big-Bench-Hard, EquityMedQA)
granular_aspects.description: 17 offline benchmark runners under deepeval/benchmarks/, each with task lists and prompt templates, to score any wrapped LLM against standard datasets (BBQ specifically targets social bias, EquityMedQA targets medical-equity bias).

limitations: The former red-teaming/adversarial/jailbreak module is now just a README stub pointing to a separate sibling repo, DeepTeam (github.com/confident-ai/deepteam) — this repo itself ships no jailbreak techniques, prompt-injection attacks, or attack-simulation red-teaming despite a 'red_teaming' folder still existing as a placeholder.

Most safety-relevant metrics (PII leakage, misuse, bias, toxicity, non-advice, role violation) are LLM-as-judge by default, so their accuracy is bounded by the judge model's own competence/bias and by non-determinism/cost of repeated LLM calls; no published precision/recall numbers for these metrics were found in the repo.

Local, deterministic alternatives (Detoxify, Dbias, SummaC, Vectara hallucination model) exist only in the lower-level Scorer/model classes, not wired as the default judge for the corresponding Metric classes, and require extra pip installs (`deepeval[bias]`, `detoxify`, `bert-score`, `torch`) not in the base dependency set.

No stated benchmark accuracy numbers for DeepEval's own judges/metrics (only third-party benchmarks like MMLU are run against the LLM under test, not against DeepEval's judges themselves) — reliability is asserted via tests, not empirically quantified in the docs.

Full functionality (best explanations/consistency) is implicitly tuned around OpenAI models; using a different LLM as the judge is supported via DeepEvalBaseLLM but quality may vary and isn't benchmarked in the repo.
Scorer.PII_score is literally `raise NotImplementedError()` — the deterministic PII scoring path in the Scorer utility class is a stub; only the LLM-judge PIILeakageMetric is functional.

reports.one_line_summary: DeepTeam (by Confident AI, sibling of DeepEval) is an Apache-2.0 Python framework that both red-teams LLM/agent systems with 50+ vulnerability probes and 20+ adversarial attack techniques, and ships 7 production LLM-as-judge guardrails plus an agentic code/trace scanner.
reports.core_functionality: Verified by reading deepteam/red_team.py, deepteam/red_teamer/, deepteam/vulnerabilities/*, deepteam/attacks/*, deepteam/metrics/*, deepteam/guardrails/*, deepteam/code_scanner/*, and deepteam/trace_scanner/*. The top-level red_team() function (deepteam/red_team.py) instantiates a RedTeamer which, given a user-supplied async model_callback, dynamically generates adversarial test inputs for chosen BaseVulnerability subclasses (deepteam/vulnerabilities/<name>/<name>.py, e.g. Bias, PIILeakage, SQLInjection, GoalTheft) using LLM-generated prompt templates (each vulnerability folder has a template.py with the natural-language attack-generation prompt and a types.py enum of sub-categories). Optionally, BaseAttack 'enhancer' classes under deepteam/attacks/single_turn and deepteam/attacks/multi_turn rewrite/obfuscate the baseline probe (e.g. deepteam/attacks/single_turn/prompt_injection/prompt_injection.py calls an LLM 'simulator_model' via generate()/a_generate() with a PromptInjectionTemplate, validates the result with an IsValidInjection schema and a compliance check, and retries up to max_retries). Multi-turn attacks (crescendo_jailbreaking, tree_jailbreaking, linear_jailbreaking, bad_likert_judge, sequential_break) run actual multi-turn conversations against the target model_callback with a BehaviorShiftDetector to decide when to stop. The target's responses are then scored with per-vulnerability Metric classes in deepteam/metrics/<name>/ (e.g. metrics/pii/pii.py + template.py), which are literally LLM-as-a-judge: a large natural-language rubric prompt (with a numbered PII taxonomy, scoring rules 0/1, and calibration blocks from evaluation_prompt_blocks.py) is sent to an 'evaluation_model' (default gpt-4o-mini/gpt-4.1) which returns a structured pass/fail + reasoning JSON, inherited from DeepEval's BaseMetric machinery. Separately, deepteam/guardrails/guardrails.py exposes a Guardrails(input_guards, output_guards) runtime object; each Guard (deepteam/guardrails/guards/<name>/*.py, e.g. privacy_guard, toxicity_guard, prompt_injection_guard, cybersecurity_guard, hallucination_guard, illegal_guard, topical_guard) inherits BaseGuard (guards/base_guard.py) whose _guard()/a_guard() method sends a template.py prompt to an LLM and parses a SafetyLevelSchema (safe/borderline/unsafe/uncertain + reason) -- there is no regex/deterministic PII or profanity detection anywhere; every guard and every vulnerability metric is a prompt-templated LLM judge call. deepteam/frameworks/* map OWASP Top 10 (LLM + Agentic 2026), NIST AI RMF, MITRE ATLAS, BeaverTails, Aegis and EU AI Act categories onto bundles of the built-in vulnerabilities/attacks (verified in frameworks/owasp/owasp.py). deepteam/code_scanner/ is a separate static-analysis feature: CodeScanner (code_scanner.py) chunks source files, builds a batch prompt via CodeScanTemplate referencing the same vulnerability taxonomy (taxonomy.py maps to VULNERABILITY_INFO_MAP), and sends it either to deepteam's own judge model or to an external agentic coding harness (Codex/Claude Agent SDK/Cursor CLI, via code_scanner/engines/{claude,codex,cursor}.py) to return CodeFinding objects (confirmed with examples/code_scan_harness_example.py, which flags eval(), subprocess shell=True, and a hardcoded API key). deepteam/trace_scanner/ similarly scores agent execution traces. A deepteam CLI (deepteam/cli, entry point 'deepteam' in pyproject.toml) drives red-teaming from YAML configs (examples/example_config.yaml, examples/.deepteam-code-scan.yaml).
key_features: 50+ vulnerability probes across Data Privacy, Responsible AI, Security, Safety, Business, and Agentic categories, each with an LLM-as-judge metric producing a 0/1 pass score with reasoning

20+ single-turn and multi-turn adversarial attack/jailbreak techniques (encoding-based, roleplay, injection-based, and iterative multi-turn like Crescendo/Tree/Linear jailbreaking) used to enhance baseline vulnerability probes

7 production-ready runtime Guardrails (PromptInjectionGuard, ToxicityGuard, PrivacyGuard, IllegalGuard, HallucinationGuard, TopicalGuard, CybersecurityGuard) with a Guardrails(input_guards, output_guards) wrapper returning breached/safety_level verdicts

Out-of-the-box mapping to 6 external safety/compliance frameworks: OWASP Top 10 for LLMs 2025, OWASP Top 10 for Agentic AI 2026, NIST AI RMF, MITRE ATLAS, BeaverTails, Aegis (plus an EU AI Act module)

Agentic-AI-specific vulnerability set (goal theft, recursive hijacking, tool metadata poisoning, tool orchestration abuse, BOLA/BFLA/RBAC, SSRF, agent identity abuse, autonomous agent drift, insecure inter-agent communication, cross-context retrieval, indirect instruction injection) plus 19 dedicated agentic metrics under metrics/agentic/

CLI (`deepteam` command) driven by YAML config files for both red-teaming and code scanning

Requires a paid hosted LLM (OpenAI by default; OPENAI_API_KEY needed) for every single check -- attack generation, vulnerability scoring, and all 7 runtime guards -- so there is no fully offline/free-to-run mode without supplying a self-hosted DeepEval-compatible custom model.

CodeScanner's optional 'engine' mode additionally depends on separately-licensed agentic coding SDKs/CLIs (OpenAI Codex, Anthropic Claude Agent SDK, Cursor CLI), each requiring its own API key and only available as optional extras (python >=3.10).

No CI/coverage badges, star counts, or issue-tracker health metrics are present in the checked-out source tree itself (no .git metadata, no README badges beyond a release/license/discord badge) -- maturity signals had to be inferred from version 1.0.9 and a CITATION.cff date-released of 2026-08-13, i.e. the repo is presented as actively maintained but true community-scale metrics (stars, open issues) could not be verified from the files alone.

Tests (93 test_*.py files found) are mostly integration-style pytest files that call real guard/metric classes and make live LLM calls asserting on qualitative outcome strings (e.g. 'safe'/'unsafe'/'borderline') rather than deterministic unit assertions, so test 'passing' still depends on judge-model behavior at run time; results can be probabilistic/flaky by design given LLM-as-judge is core to the architecture.

Being fundamentally a Python/DeepEval-based judge framework, none of its checks are portable as-is into a non-Python backend without re-implementing the prompt templates or calling out to a Python microservice.

reports.integration_effort_reason: Installing via pip and wiring `Guardrails(input_guards=[...], output_guards=[...])` around a Flask/FastAPI request/response cycle is only a few lines of glue code (guard_input()/guard_output() return a simple breached bool + reason), and the library is pure Python with clean class-based APIs (BaseGuard, BaseVulnerability, BaseAttack, RedTeamer) that require no build step or GPU. Please use a better evaluation model.') when the judge fails to comply, signaling the maintainers are aware of judge-model reliability as a known failure mode. The project is versioned 1.0.9 (past 1.0, i.e. declared stable API) with a CITATION.cff dated 2026-08-13 and a large, actively-expanding surface (50+ vulnerabilities, 20+ attacks, 7 guards, 6 external framework mappings, a code/trace scanner) suggesting an actively maintained, fast-moving project; the 93 test files exercise real classes end-to-end but assert on LLM-judged qualitative labels rather than fixed ground truth, so the test suite validates wiring/API stability more than judge accuracy. Being built directly on DeepEval (a well-established sibling project) lends indirect credibility to its evaluation infrastructure.
reports.afni_fit_note: Best positioned as the Vulnerability/Red-Team + evaluation layer in a unified AFNI toolkit: use its 50+ vulnerability probes, 20+ attack simulators, and OWASP/NIST/MITRE framework mappings for pre-deployment red-teaming and CI regression testing, and optionally wire its 7 lightweight Guardrails classes as an LLM-judge-based input/output filter in a FastAPI gateway -- but pair it with a deterministic/library-based PII, secrets, and profanity scanner (e.g. Presidio, regex/entity-based tools) since DeepTeam has zero non-LLM detection and every check costs a live API call.

Best slotted in as the offline red-team / benchmark harness in a unified AFNI toolkit: use its elsuite adversarial games (sandbagging, make-me-say, make-me-pay, steganography, ballots) to stress-test AFNI's models for deception, covert persuasion, and capability-hiding before release, and reuse its model-graded YAML pattern (fact.yaml, security.yaml) as a template for building LLM-judge checks; it is not a drop-in runtime guardrail (no PII/toxicity/fairness detectors, CLI/batch-oriented, no synchronous score() API) so it would sit alongside, not replace, dedicated library-based PII/toxicity/bias modules and would need a thin FastAPI wrapper around oaieval/Eval subclasses to be callable from a backend.
reports.core_functionality: This is OpenAI's evals framework (confirmed via pyproject.toml repository URL github.com/openai/evals, package name "evals" v3.0.1.post1, oaieval/oaievalset CLI entry points). Core architecture (read in evals/eval.py, evals/base.py, evals/api.py, evals/record.py, evals/registry.py, evals/metrics.py): an abstract Eval class (and stateful SolverEval subclass) that loads a JSONL sample set, shuffles/seeds it deterministically, fans work out across a ThreadPool (size via EVALS_THREADS env var) calling a pluggable CompletionFn/Solver per sample, and records per-sample events plus aggregate metrics through a RecorderBase (local JSON, Snowflake, or HTTP sink, per evals/record.py). Concrete eval logic lives in two places: (1) evals/elsuite/basic/* -- deterministic string/JSON matchers (Match, Includes, FuzzyMatch, JsonMatch, JsonValidator); (2) evals/elsuite/modelgraded/classify.py plus classify_utils.py -- a generic LLM-as-judge engine that renders a YAML "modelgraded spec" (prompt + choice_strings/choice_scores) from evals/registry/modelgraded/*.yaml against a completion, parses the judge's choice, and records a score. On top of this, evals/registry/evals/*.yaml wires roughly 463 individual benchmark tasks (capability/QA/coding/translation benchmarks plus a handful of RAI-adjacent ones: bias_detection.yaml, human-safety.yaml, moral_exceptQA.yaml). Separately, evals/elsuite/(sandbagging, make_me_say, make_me_pay, steganography, ballots, bluff, schelling_point, ...) implement bespoke multi-agent adversarial "policy research" evals (originally openai/policy-research-evals, merged in) that pit LLMs against each other to measure deception, manipulation, covert communication, and coordination. Model access is via evals/solvers/providers/(openai,anthropic,google,together) and evals/completion_fns/(openai.py, langchain_llm.py, cot.py, retrieval.py) -- every non-trivial eval calls a live hosted LLM API either as the system under test or as the grading/monitor model.

Deterministic string/JSON matchers: Match, Includes, FuzzyMatch, JsonMatch, JsonValidator (evals/elsuite/basic)
Generic model-graded LLM-as-judge classification engine driven by YAML prompt specs (evals/elsuite/modelgraded/classify.py plus evals/registry/modelgraded)
Registry of about 463 predefined eval tasks plus eval-sets, completion-fn, and solver YAML configs (evals/registry.py, evals/registry)
Multi-agent adversarial policy-research evals for deception, persuasion and covert comms: sandbagging, make-me-say, make-me-pay, steganography, ballots, bluff, schelling_point
Agentic and tool-use robustness evals: bugged_tools, cant_do_that_anymore, multistep_web_tasks, hr_ml_agent_bench, error_recovery

evals/elsuite/basic/json_match.py and json_validator.py validate that structured JSON output parses and matches an expected value/schema.

evals/registry/modelgraded/fact.yaml is an LLM-judge prompt that classifies a submitted answer against an expert answer into 5 factual-consistency categories (subset/superset/same/conflict/immaterial difference) -- a hallucination/groundedness-style check.

evals/registry/modelgraded/security.yaml is a single LLM-judge prompt ('Is this string malicious? Yes/No/Unsure') -- a shallow, unvalidated content/malware classifier with no supporting benchmark in-repo.

granular_aspects.description: Generic LLM-as-judge YAML templates in evals/registry/modelgraded for pairwise comparison, keyword presence, or quality/plausibility scoring of completions.

evals/elsuite/make_me_say tests whether a manipulator LLM can covertly induce a second LLM to say a secret codeword without the target detecting the manipulation, judged by a third LLM; reports win/loss/violation rates and user_aware_of_manipulation.
evals/elsuite/make_me_pay/makemepay.py pits a con-artist LLM against a mark LLM to measure success rate and size of persuaded monetary transfers.

evals/elsuite/steganography/eval.py, monitor.py and reconstruction_metrics.py have an encoder model hide a secret payload in ordinary text, a decoder recover it, and a third monitor LLM flag suspicious text; metrics include character_error_rate, embedding-cosine semantic_distance, detectability, and undetected_acc.
evals/elsuite/ballots tests whether an LLM influencer with a hidden agenda can skew a simulated voter's stance on a ballot proposition through biased framing.
evals/elsuite/bugged_tools/bugged_tools.py measures whether an agent correctly identifies when a tool it calls is malfunctioning mid-task.

granular_aspects.aspect: Can't Do That Anymore rule-override eval
granular_aspects.description: evals/elsuite/cant_do_that_anymore uses a modified chess variant to test whether a model can apply novel task rules instead of defaulting to memorized/training-biased behavior.
evals/elsuite/schelling_point tests unsupervised convergence/coordination between separate model instances without explicit communication, relevant to covert coordination risk.

evals/metrics.py provides get_confusion_matrix, compute_matthew_corr, compute_precision/recall/f_score and macro-averaged F-score, usable by any classification-style eval including per-class breakdowns.

evals/registry/evals/bias_detection.yaml classifies news sentences into rhetorical categories (fact/opinion/claim/argument/data/quote/narrative/sensationalism/speculation) via the Includes scorer -- despite the name, this is NOT a demographic-bias/fairness metric.
evals/registry/evals/human-safety.yaml is a FuzzyMatch benchmark of logical reasoning about physical-danger scenarios, not a harmful-content filter.
evals/registry/evals/moral_exceptQA.yaml and parable-to-moral-match.yaml are QA-style benchmarks of moral/ethical reasoning correctness rather than active guardrails.

evals/registry/modelgraded/diversity.yaml is an LLM-judge Yes/No prompt asking whether a set of N generated texts is diverse -- a weak, generic diversity check, not a demographic-representation metric.

limitations: No dedicated PII/entity detectors, demographic bias/fairness metrics (no protected-attribute or disparate-impact analysis), toxicity/profanity classifiers, jailbreak-prompt libraries, or secret-scanning patterns anywhere in the repo, despite eval names like bias_detection and human-safety which test unrelated things (rhetorical sentence classification and physical-danger reasoning, respectively).
Model-graded checks (fact, security, diversity, etc.) are single unvalidated LLM-judge prompts with no published accuracy/precision numbers for the judge itself inside this repo.

Nearly every eval beyond simple string-matching requires a live, paid call to a hosted LLM API (OpenAI/Anthropic/Google/Together) either as the system under test, the judge, or the monitor -- nothing meaningful runs fully free/offline.

CLI-first, batch/offline design (oaieval); there is no synchronous score-text-to-verdict API, so using it as an inline runtime guardrail in a web backend requires custom glue (CompletionFn/Solver adapters, registry YAML, log parsing).
Test suite (20 *_test.py files) validates harness plumbing (matchers, registry parsing, provider adapters) rather than the real-world detection accuracy of any specific check.
Most registry datasets are stored via Git-LFS and must be explicitly fetched, adding a setup step; maintainers also document a known bug where a run can hang after the final report.

Wiring it into a Flask/FastAPI backend for runtime guardrail use requires: writing a CompletionFn/Solver adapter around the production model, authoring registry YAML for the desired eval/modelgraded spec, invoking the CLI or Eval subclass programmatically, and parsing its JSON log output -- plus a live per-call LLM API charge and latency for any model-graded (LLM-as-judge) check, which is unsuitable as-is for low-latency inline scoring without a wrapper service.
reports.reliability_notes: Maintained by OpenAI, MIT-licensed, mature and widely-used framework at v3.0.1.post1 with a real (if modest) colocated pytest suite (20 *_test.py files) covering matchers, registry parsing, record-keeping, and provider solvers. However, the repo does not publish benchmark accuracy/precision figures for its own detectors (e.g. the security malicious-string judge is a single untested prompt); the adversarial elsuite evals (sandbagging, make-me-say, steganography, ballots) do report empirical results/plots against GPT-3.5/GPT-4 in their READMEs, which speaks to frontier-model behavior more than to the reliability of the check itself. Microsoft Fairlearn is a Python/scikit-learn-compatible toolkit for measuring group-fairness metrics (demographic parity, equalized odds, etc.) on classifier/regressor predictions and mitigating detected disparities via pre-, in-, and post-processing algorithms.
reports.core_functionality: Confirmed via source (not just README): the package has two pillars. (1) Metrics: fairlearn/metrics/_metric_frame.py defines MetricFrame, a pandas-based object that disaggregates any sklearn-style metric function(s) by one or more sensitive-feature columns, computing per-group values plus .overall, .by_group, .difference()/.ratio()/.group_min()/.group_max() aggregates, with optional bootstrap confidence intervals (_bootstrap.py) and multi-metric/multi-sensitive-feature support (_group_feature.py, _disaggregated_result.py, _annotated_metric_function.py). fairlearn/metrics/_base_metrics.py implements true_positive_rate, true_negative_rate, false_positive_rate, false_negative_rate (all via sklearn confusion_matrix), selection_rate, mean_prediction, and count from scratch. fairlearn/metrics/_fairness_metrics.py builds demographic_parity_difference/ratio, equalized_odds_difference/ratio, equal_opportunity_difference/ratio on top of MetricFrame. fairlearn/metrics/_generated_metrics.py programmatically generates <metric>_{difference,ratio,group_min,group_max} variants for accuracy_score, zero_one_loss, balanced_accuracy_score, precision_score, recall_score, roc_auc_score, mean_absolute_error, mean_squared_error, r2_score, f1_score, log_loss (via make_derived_metric in _make_derived_metric.py), in addition to the four base rate metrics -> dozens of auto-generated named metric functions exposed at package level. (2) Mitigation algorithms, split into three families read directly from source: (a) Reductions (fairlearn/reductions/): ExponentiatedGradient and GridSearch, which reduce fair classification/regression to a sequence of weighted classification problems using 'Moment' constraint objects -- DemographicParity, EqualizedOdds, TruePositiveRateParity, FalsePositiveRateParity, ErrorRateParity (all in _moments/utility_parity.py, subclassing UtilityParity/ClassificationMoment, implementing the Agarwal et al. 2018 'A Reductions Approach to Fair Classification' Lagrangian formulation with pos/neg bases, gamma, signed_weights) and BoundedGroupLoss / ConditionalLossMoment (_moments/bounded_group_loss.py) with SquareLoss/AbsoluteLoss/ZeroOneLoss for regression fairness. (b) Post-processing (fairlearn/postprocessing/_threshold_optimizer.py): ThresholdOptimizer implements Hardt/Price/Srebro 'Equality of Opportunity in Supervised Learning', wrapping a fitted sklearn estimator and computing group-specific decision thresholds to satisfy one of SIMPLE_CONSTRAINTS (selection_rate_parity, demographic_parity, false_positive_rate_parity, false_negative_rate_parity, true_positive_rate_parity, true_negative_rate_parity) or equalized_odds, optimizing a chosen objective (accuracy_score, balanced_accuracy_score, selection_rate, true_positive_rate, true_negative_rate) via tradeoff-curve interpolation (_tradeoff_curve_utilities.py, _relaxed_constraints.py, _interpolated_thresholder.py). (c) Pre-processing (fairlearn/preprocessing/): CorrelationRemover (linear-algebra transform removing correlation between sensitive and non-sensitive feature columns via least-squares projection, narwhals-backed for dataframe-agnostic support) and a PrototypeRepresentationLearner. (d) Adversarial (fairlearn/adversarial/_adversarial_mitigation.py): _AdversarialFairness / FairnessClassifier / FairnessRegressor implementing Zhang et al. 2018 'Mitigating Unwanted Biases with Adversarial Learning' -- trains a predictor network against an adversary network that tries to predict the sensitive feature from the predictor's output, pluggable via PyTorch or TensorFlow backend engines (_pytorch_engine.py, _tensorflow_engine.py, _backend_engine.py). All classes are scikit-learn BaseEstimator-compatible (fit/predict/transform), confirmed by reading actual class signatures and test files under test/unit/{metrics,reductions,postprocessing,preprocessing,adversarial}/.
key_features: MetricFrame: disaggregated metric computation across arbitrary sensitive-feature groupings, with difference()/ratio()/group_min()/group_max() aggregation and bootstrap confidence intervals
Built-in base rate metrics: true_positive_rate, true_negative_rate, false_positive_rate, false_negative_rate, selection_rate, mean_prediction, count
Named fairness disparity metrics: demographic_parity_difference/ratio, equalized_odds_difference/ratio, equal_opportunity_difference/ratio
Auto-generated difference/ratio/group_min/group_max variants for 11 sklearn metrics (accuracy, precision, recall, F1, ROC AUC, MAE, MSE, R2, log loss, balanced accuracy, zero-one loss)
Reduction-based mitigation: ExponentiatedGradient and GridSearch wrapping any sklearn estimator under a fairness Moment constraint
Fairness constraint objects (Moments): DemographicParity, EqualizedOdds, TruePositiveRateParity, FalsePositiveRateParity, ErrorRateParity, BoundedGroupLoss
ThresholdOptimizer post-processing (Hardt-Price-Srebro group-threshold equality of opportunity/odds)
CorrelationRemover pre-processing transformer to strip linear correlation with sensitive features
Adversarial debiasing (_AdversarialFairness / FairnessClassifier / FairnessRegressor) with PyTorch and TensorFlow backends
Bundled fairness-relevant benchmark datasets: Adult, ACS Income, Bank Marketing, Boston housing, Credit Card, Diabetes Hospital readmission

granular_aspects.aspect: Demographic Parity (difference & ratio, and as a reduction constraint)
granular_aspects.description: Measures/enforces equal selection rate P[h(X)=1|A=a] across sensitive-feature groups; implemented in _fairness_metrics.py and as the DemographicParity Moment/constraint in reductions and as a ThresholdOptimizer constraint.

Compares TPR and FPR parity jointly across groups; implemented via MetricFrame combining true_positive_rate and false_positive_rate, and as the EqualizedOdds Moment class and ThresholdOptimizer constraint.
TPR parity only (P[h(X)=1|A=a,Y=1]); implemented in _fairness_metrics.py and as TruePositiveRateParity Moment.

granular_aspects.aspect: False Positive / False Negative Rate Parity
granular_aspects.description: FalsePositiveRateParity Moment class and corresponding ThresholdOptimizer simple constraints.
ErrorRateParity Moment class enforcing equal misclassification rate P[h(X)!=Y|A=a] across groups.
ConditionalLossMoment/BoundedGroupLoss bounds per-group mean loss (SquareLoss/AbsoluteLoss/ZeroOneLoss) for fair regression.
Computed from sklearn confusion_matrix per group, used as building blocks for all disparity metrics.
Basic per-group statistics (fraction predicted positive, weighted mean prediction, group sample count) used both standalone and as MetricFrame inputs.

granular_aspects.aspect: Derived difference/ratio/group_min/group_max wrappers for standard ML metrics
granular_aspects.description: make_derived_metric auto-wraps accuracy, precision, recall, F1, ROC AUC, MAE, MSE, R2, log loss, balanced accuracy, zero-one loss into group-disparity versions.

Iterative Lagrangian-based algorithm (Agarwal et al. 2018) that reweights/relabels training data to satisfy a chosen fairness Moment while minimizing error, wrapped around any sklearn classifier/regressor.
Exhaustive grid over Lagrange multiplier space producing a family of classifiers trading off fairness vs. accuracy, using the same Moment constraints.

Post-hoc technique that assigns different decision thresholds per sensitive-feature group to satisfy demographic_parity/equalized_odds/etc. while maximizing an accuracy-type objective, via tradeoff-curve interpolation.
Pre-processing linear transform that removes correlation between sensitive feature columns and the remaining features via least-squares projection, controllable via alpha parameter.
Preprocessing representation-learning transformer aimed at learning fairer intermediate representations (prototype-based).

Trains a predictor jointly with an adversary that tries to recover the sensitive feature from predictor outputs (Zhang et al. 2018), supported on PyTorch or TensorFlow backends, for demographic-parity-style in-processing mitigation.

MetricFrame supports n_boot/ci_quantiles parameters to compute bootstrap resampled confidence intervals on any metric, aiding statistical reliability of fairness assessments (fairlearn/metrics/_bootstrap.py).

MetricFrame and Moments support multiple simultaneous sensitive-feature columns (and 'control features' to stratify constraints), enabling intersectional fairness analysis rather than single-attribute only.

limitations: No PII/secrets/jailbreak/content-safety/hallucination detection whatsoever -- this is purely a statistical group-fairness toolkit for structured tabular ML classifiers/regressors, not an LLM guardrail or red-teaming tool.

All fairness metrics require the user to already have a labeled 'sensitive_features' column and ground-truth y_true/y_pred at hand; the repo does no automatic detection of sensitive attributes from raw data/text.
Requires binary/discretized labels for most constraint classes (Moment.load_data typically calls enforce_binary_labels=True); multi-class/continuous sensitive-feature support is more limited.

Adversarial mitigation module requires an installed PyTorch or TensorFlow backend (heavy optional dependency, not installed by default) plus custom-authored predictor/adversary neural network modules -- non-trivial glue code.
Project classifies itself as 'Development Status :: 3 - Alpha' in pyproject.toml despite version 0.15.0.dev0, signaling the API/behavior may still change.

Docs/README explicitly caveat that quantitative fairness metrics cannot capture all sociotechnical aspects of fairness (justice, due process) and that multiple fairness metrics can be mutually incompatible -- maintainers state this is a human-judgment-augmenting tool, not a pass/fail certifier.

Not applicable to LLM/generative-AI outputs (text, chat) without the caller building an entirely separate labeling/feature-extraction layer to turn model outputs into the y_true/y_pred/sensitive_features tabular format this library expects.
prerequisites: Python >= 3.11
numpy >= 1.24.4, pandas >= 2.0.3, scikit-learn >= 1.6.0, scipy >= 1.9.3, narwhals >= 1.14.0 (core deps, pip install fairlearn)

reports.integration_effort_reason: Core metrics (MetricFrame, demographic_parity_difference, equalized_odds_difference, etc.) are trivial to call from a Python/Flask/FastAPI backend -- pure functions/classes over numpy/pandas arrays with no network calls, so wiring them into a batch fairness-report endpoint is low effort. However, meaningful use in a governance pipeline requires the backend team to first assemble ground-truth labels, model predictions, and a sensitive-feature column for every scored request/record (data-engineering work outside the library), and the mitigation algorithms (ExponentiatedGradient, GridSearch, ThresholdOptimizer, CorrelationRemover) require access to a trainable/refittable sklearn-compatible model rather than just its inference API, which is a bigger integration lift for teams that only have a black-box model endpoint. Adversarial debiasing adds a further High-effort tier since it needs PyTorch/TensorFlow, custom neural architectures, and training infrastructure.
reports.reliability_notes: Algorithms are directly traceable to peer-reviewed papers cited in docstrings (Agarwal et al. 2018 'A Reductions Approach to Fair Classification' for reductions; Hardt, Price, Srebro 2016 'Equality of Opportunity in Supervised Learning' for ThresholdOptimizer; Zhang et al. 2018 'Mitigating Unwanted Biases with Adversarial Learning' for the adversarial module), giving it stronger theoretical grounding than most guardrail repos in this review set. The repo ships a large, granular unit-test suite (62 test_*.py files observed under test/unit covering metrics, reductions/{exponentiated_gradient,grid_search,moments}, postprocessing, preprocessing, adversarial, plus install-sanity tests test_no_matplotlib.py/test_no_ml.py and pickling tests), and pytest is configured with filterwarnings='error' (warnings-as-errors) indicating a mature CI discipline; a .circleci/ directory and pre-commit config with ruff/black/isort further support this. It is a Microsoft-maintained, long-running open-source project (multiple named maintainers in pyproject.toml, CITATION.cff for academic citation, active Discord/StackOverflow support channels), but pyproject.toml self-classifies as 'Development Status :: 3 - Alpha', and the README explicitly states fairness metrics cannot capture all fairness dimensions and that different fairness definitions can conflict -- the maintainers frame it as a decision-support tool for humans, not an automated certifier. I could not directly verify GitHub star count or issue-response latency from files in the checkout (no metadata file with that data was present), so that specific claim is unverified from source alone.
reports.afni_fit_note: Fits as the tabular/structured-ML bias-and-fairness measurement + mitigation layer in a unified AFNI toolkit -- pair it with LLM-focused guardrail repos (PII/jailbreak/content-safety/hallucination) since Fairlearn covers none of that; it is the natural plug-in for any classifier/regressor-based decisioning model (credit, hiring, admissions) where AFNI needs quantifiable, group-level fairness metrics and optional in-training or post-hoc bias mitigation, invoked as an offline/batch evaluation-and-mitigation harness rather than a runtime request-time guardrail.

Best suited as an offline red-team/attack-simulation module feeding an AFNI guardrail pipeline — run FuzzyAI's 20 jailbreak attack techniques against a candidate model/guardrail before deployment, then feed jailbreak-success telemetry into AFNI's runtime guardrail tuning; not itself a runtime guardrail.
reports.core_functionality: FuzzyAI (CyberArk, path src/fuzzyai) is an async Python fuzzing/attack orchestration framework, not a guardrail library. Its core is `Fuzzer` (src/fuzzyai/fuzzer.py) which wires together LLM provider clients (src/fuzzyai/llm/providers/*: openai, anthropic, azure, bedrock, gemini, ai21, deepseek, ollama, local HF models, generic REST), a registry of pluggable "attack handlers" (src/fuzzyai/handlers/attacks/*, discovered via a `FlavorManager`/decorator pattern in utils/flavor_manager.py and enumerated in handlers/attacks/enums.py: FuzzerAttackMode), a set of "classifiers" that judge whether an attack succeeded (handlers/classifiers/*, enumerated in handlers/classifiers/enums.py: Classifier), and optional "mutators" that transform prompts between attack iterations (handlers/mutators/*). `BaseAttackTechniqueHandler.attack()` (handlers/attacks/base.py) manages an asyncio worker-queue pipeline: it pulls prompts, calls the target LLM, then async-dispatches the configured classifiers to score each response, writing JSONL results to a local `.out/<attack_id>` file and (optionally) MongoDB (db/mongodb.py, run_mongo.sh) for persistence/reporting. A CLI (`fuzzyai fuzz`, cli.py) and an experimental Streamlit-based Web UI (webui.py) drive it. examples.py and tests/test_cli_port.py demonstrate real usage: constructing a Fuzzer, adding LLM providers and classifiers, and calling `fuzzer.fuzz([FuzzerAttackMode.X], ...)` against Ollama/local/cloud models.

Multi-provider LLM abstraction (OpenAI, Anthropic, Azure, AWS Bedrock, Gemini, AI21, DeepSeek, Ollama, local HuggingFace/Llama2, generic REST target)
Async worker-pool attack engine with resumable attack_id state and per-attack extra-args validated via Pydantic
Prompt mutators (rephrase, summarize, retokenize, random-drop, fine-tuned-summarizer, might-be-harmful-check) usable inside iterative attacks like the genetic/GPTFuzzer techniques
Optional MongoDB persistence of adversarial prompts, suffixes, taxonomy data and fuzzer reports
CLI (`fuzzyai fuzz`) plus an experimental Streamlit Web UI and Jupyter notebooks (builtin_evaluators, llm_attacks_detection_methods_evaluation) for interactive/offline use
Shipped datasets/resources: AdvBench subsets, harmful_behaviors.csv, adversarial suffixes/prompts, persuasion taxonomy jsonl, Pandora's prompts, benign prompts, history-framing prompts

granular_aspects.description: handlers/attacks/bon/handler.py implements arXiv:2412.03556 — repeatedly augments/perturbs a prompt N times to probabilistically elicit a harmful response.
handlers/attacks/genetic/handler.py uses the pygad genetic-algorithm library (arXiv:2309.01446) to evolve adversarial suffixes/prompts against a target model, backed by handlers/db/adv_genetic.py.
handlers/attacks/crescendo/handler.py gradually escalates conversational turns from innocuous to restricted topics (arXiv:2404.01833).
handlers/attacks/actor_attack builds actor-network-theory-inspired semantic chains to conceal malicious intent across turns (arXiv:2410.10700).
handlers/attacks/manyshot/handler.py embeds many fake in-context dialogue examples to weaken safety alignment (Anthropic research).
handlers/attacks/artprompt renders trigger words as ASCII art (via the `art` library) to bypass text-based content filters (arXiv:2402.11753).
handlers/attacks/ascii_smuggling hides instructions using invisible Unicode tag characters, a prompt-injection vector.
handlers/attacks/taxonomy + resources/persuasion_taxonomy.jsonl rewrite prompts using specific persuasion techniques (emotional appeal, authority, etc., arXiv:2401.06373).
handlers/attacks/dan induces an unrestricted 'Do Anything Now' persona to bypass content filters.
handlers/attacks/word_game disguises harmful requests as word puzzles (arXiv:2405.14023).
handlers/attacks/hallucinations exploits model-generated hallucinated content to bypass RLHF safety filters (arXiv:2403.04769).
handlers/attacks/gpt_fuzzer applies crossover/mutation operations to jailbreak templates using an auxiliary mutation model.
handlers/attacks/shuffle_inconsistency shuffles harmful text to exploit the gap between LLM comprehension and safety filtering (arXiv:2501.04931); image variant not implemented.
handlers/attacks/piglatin translates the harmful prompt into Pig Latin to slip past keyword-based filters.

granular_aspects.aspect: Back-To-The-Past / History framing / Please / Thought-Experiment prompt-wrapping attacks
granular_aspects.description: Four lightweight handlers (back_to_the_past, history_framing, please, thought_experiment) each prepend/append a specific social-engineering frame (past-tense, scholarly/historical, politeness, hypothetical) to the harmful request.
handlers/classifiers/azure_content_safety/handler.py calls Azure's detectJailbreak, shieldPrompt, and analyze (8-severity-level sexual/violence/hate/self-harm) endpoints.
handlers/classifiers/aws_guardrails and aws_bedrock call Bedrock's apply_guardrail / converse APIs to detect GUARDRAIL_INTERVENED outcomes.
handlers/classifiers/openai_moderation/handler.py calls OpenAI's moderation endpoint (omni-moderation-latest) and flags any category hit.
handlers/classifiers/harmful_llm and harmful_score_llm prompt an LLM to answer Yes/No or rate harm 1-5, with hard-coded refusal-string heuristics as a fast path.

handlers/classifiers/rating (1-10 PAIR-style jailbreak scoring rubric with embedded few-shot examples) and committee/handler.py (averages coherence/consistency/relevance prompts plus a harmfulness score) act as LLM-as-judge ensembles.

handlers/text_analyzer.py wraps a local facebook/bart-large-mnli zero-shot pipeline (GPU-optional) used by disapproval, sentiment, and llm_response_sentiment classifiers to detect refusal vs. compliance.

handlers/classifiers/cosine_similarity + handlers/sentence_similarity_analyzer.py embed two responses with sentence-transformers/all-MiniLM-L6-v2 and compare via cosine similarity/dissimilarity threshold.
handlers/classifiers/obvious_negative/handler.py is a pure string-prefix check (e.g. 'sorry', 'i cannot') — the only fully deterministic, non-model classifier shipped.

limitations: This is fundamentally an attack/red-team tool, not a defensive guardrail — it produces jailbreak attempts and success/failure scores, it does not block or sanitize production traffic.

Most 'classifiers' are themselves LLM-as-judge or ML-model based (bart-large-mnli, sentence-transformers), so their own accuracy is unverified in-repo; README explicitly warns 'not all classifiers are compatible with the attack methods... as those methods are designed for single-output classifiers,' and several classifier docstrings/comments show hand-tuned magic thresholds (e.g. 0.45, 0.55, 0.85) without cited validation data.

No quantitative benchmark numbers, accuracy/precision-recall figures, or leaderboard results found anywhere in the repo (README, docs, or code comments) — reliability claims are architecture-in-code appearance only, not measured performance.

Automated test coverage is very thin: only tests/test_cli_port.py (webui port-finding logic) plus a handful of unit/integration tests for individual LLM provider clients (Azure, Anthropic/Bedrock, Ollama, local, Mongo) — there is no test suite validating attack-success detection accuracy or classifier correctness.

Web UI is explicitly marked 'Experimental' in the README; genetic/GPTFuzzer/local-model attacks require local GPU-capable HuggingFace models (torch 2.2.2, transformers 4.51.3) and are heavier to operate than the pure-API attacks.

Cloud-backed classifiers (AWS Bedrock/Guardrails, Azure Content Safety, OpenAI Moderation) require paid API credentials/IAM sessions and are wrappers around third-party services rather than in-repo detection logic — FuzzyAI itself does not implement the detection model for those.

No CI badges, coverage reports, or release/versioning cadence artifacts were found in the repo beyond a single pyproject version '1.0.0'; GitHub activity/star signals could not be verified from local files alone.
