reports.core_functionality: SHAP (SHapley Additive exPlanations) computes game-theoretic Shapley-value feature attributions for any ML model's predictions. shap/explainers/_explainer.py defines the top-level Explainer(model, masker, link, algorithm=...) dispatcher that auto-selects a concrete algorithm subclass; concrete implementations live in shap/explainers/_tree.py (exact/fast Tree SHAP for XGBoost/LightGBM/CatBoost/sklearn/pyspark, backed by a compiled C extension in shap/cext/tree_shap.h and _cext.cc, plus optional GPU code in _cext_gpu.cu / _gpu_tree.py), _kernel.py (model-agnostic weighted linear-regression approximation of Shapley values), _deep.py (DeepLIFT-style backprop for TF/PyTorch), _gradient.py, _linear.py, _partition.py/_permutation.py/_sampling.py/_exact.py/_additive.py/_coalition.py. Masking of "hidden" features is handled by shap/maskers/ (_tabular.py, _text.py, _image.py, _composite.py) which define how features are perturbed/removed to estimate marginal contributions. shap/models/ wraps callable prediction functions, including transformer text-generation/teacher-forcing wrappers (_text_generation.py, _teacher_forcing.py, _transformers_pipeline.py) for NLP explanation use cases. shap/_explanation.py defines the Explanation/Cohorts result objects returned by every explainer. shap/plots/ (bar, beeswarm, waterfall, force, heatmap, scatter, text, _group_difference.py) renders the attributions; _group_difference.py explicitly computes mean SHAP-value differences between two sample groups with bootstrap confidence intervals as a way to decompose fairness/parity metrics by feature. shap/benchmark/ (measures.py, metrics.py, _sequential.py, _explanation_error.py) is a separate offline evaluation harness that scores explanation *methods themselves* (not model outputs) via metrics like local_accuracy, consistency_guarantees, runtime, and remove/keep-and-retrain "faithfulness" tests. I read shap/__init__.py, explainers/__init__.py, explainers/_explainer.py, benchmark/metrics.py, benchmark/measures.py, plots/_group_difference.py, pyproject.toml, and tests/explainers/test_kernel.py (which shows the canonical usage pattern: fit an sklearn SVM, build shap.KernelExplainer(model.predict_proba, X_train), call .shap_values(X_test), then shap.force_plot(...)). The repo ships 55 test_*.py files across tests/explainers, tests/maskers, tests/plots, tests/benchmark, tests/actions, tests/models, tests/utils.

granular_aspects.description: Polynomial-time exact Shapley value computation for tree ensembles (XGBoost/LightGBM/CatBoost/sklearn/pyspark) via shap/explainers/_tree.py and the C++ backend in shap/cext/tree_shap.h.

Model-agnostic, weighted local linear regression approximation of Shapley values (shap/explainers/_kernel.py) usable on any black-box function.
DeepLIFT-based backpropagation approximation of Shapley values for TensorFlow/Keras and PyTorch models (shap/explainers/_deep/).
Gradient-based Shapley approximation combining ideas from Integrated Gradients and SHAP (shap/explainers/_gradient.py).
Closed-form exact SHAP values for linear and generalized additive models (shap/explainers/_linear.py, _additive.py).

granular_aspects.description: Alternative estimation strategies trading off exactness vs. speed, including hierarchical-clustering-aware Owen values (Partition) and brute-force Exact enumeration.

granular_aspects.description: shap/models/_text_generation.py, _teacher_forcing.py, _topk_lm.py, _transformers_pipeline.py wrap Hugging Face pipelines so token-level SHAP explanations can be produced for classification and generative language models.
shap/maskers/_image.py and shap/utils/image.py support superpixel/patch-level masking for explaining CNN and vision-transformer predictions.

shap/plots/_group_difference.py decomposes the mean difference in model output (or SHAP values) between two sample groups (e.g., protected vs. non-protected) into per-feature contributions with bootstrap confidence bounds -- a diagnostic building block for disparate-impact analysis, not a bias metric library itself.

shap/benchmark/metrics.py + measures.py implement local_accuracy, consistency_guarantees, runtime, and remove/keep-and-retrain (comparing model degradation when top/bottom attributed features are masked and the model is retrained or imputed) as offline metrics to judge whether an attribution method's explanations are trustworthy.
shap/actions/_optimizer.py searches for minimal, low-cost feature changes that flip a model decision, given a cost function per action -- supports actionable-recourse / accountability workflows.

limitations: Not a security/PII/jailbreak/content-safety tool at all -- it is purely a model-explainability (feature attribution) library; any RAI checklist mapping must route it only to the Explainability/Transparency (and secondarily Fairness support / Accountability) tenets.

No built-in bias/fairness metrics (no demographic parity, equalized odds, disparate impact computation) -- shap/plots/_group_difference.py only visualizes per-feature SHAP differences between two user-supplied groups; the actual fairness metric and group labels must be supplied by the integrating team.

Kernel/Permutation/Sampling SHAP scale poorly (exponential/factorial-ish sampling cost in feature count) and are approximations, not exact Shapley values, for non-tree/non-linear models; correctness depends on background-data choice and number of samples.

Compiled C++/CUDA extension (shap/cext) means non-tree fast paths are pure Python and can be slow; GPU Tree SHAP requires building from source with SHAP_ENABLE_CUDA and the CUDA toolkit installed -- not a pip-install-and-go GPU path.

Deep learning explainers (_deep.py, _gradient.py) require version-matched TensorFlow/Keras or PyTorch and have known compatibility caveats (test/dependency pins in pyproject.toml exclude newer Python/TF/Torch versions), suggesting fragility across framework upgrades.

Benchmark/metrics subpackage (shap/benchmark) is explicitly for evaluating explanation *methods* against each other, not for evaluating a production model's outputs, hallucinations, or safety at runtime.

reports.integration_effort_reason: Core usage (shap.Explainer(model), explainer(X), read Explanation.values) is a handful of lines and needs no external API, GPU, or paid model -- for a Flask/FastAPI backend that already has the trained model object and a representative background dataset in-process, wiring in an /explain endpoint is straightforward. Effort rises to Medium (not Low) because: (1) it needs a live reference to the actual model/predict function plus a background dataset, which most serving APIs don't naturally keep around post-deployment, so glue code is needed to load/cache the model and data for on-demand explanation; (2) picking the right explainer/masker for non-tree models (text, image, deep nets) requires model-specific knowledge and dependency installation (torch/tensorflow/transformers); (3) SHAP computation itself can be slow (especially Kernel/Permutation SHAP) so a production integration typically needs async/background-job handling rather than synchronous request/response; (4) output is numeric arrays/plots, so the team must build their own JSON serialization and UI rendering layer on top of shap.Explanation objects.
reports.reliability_notes: Mature, widely-used project (MIT licensed, PyPI/conda-forge distributed, Production/Stable classifier in pyproject.toml, backed by peer-reviewed papers including a Nature Machine Intelligence paper for Tree SHAP and a Nature Biomedical Engineering paper for force plots). Has an extensive CI-driven test suite (55 test_*.py files spanning explainers, maskers, plots with baseline-image comparison via pytest-mpl, benchmark, actions, models, utils) plus dependabot and codecov config, indicating active maintenance and reasonably high code-quality bar. Reliability of the explanations themselves is algorithm-dependent: Tree SHAP and Linear/Additive SHAP are mathematically exact for their model classes; Kernel/Permutation/Sampling SHAP are stochastic approximations whose accuracy depends on sample count and background data choice (the repo's own benchmark/measures.py module exists precisely because approximation quality must be empirically checked). No adversarial/red-team testing of the explanations' robustness is present in this repo.
reports.one_line_summary: SHAP is a game-theoretic Python library that computes exact or approximate Shapley-value feature attributions to explain individual and aggregate predictions of any machine learning model.
A Python library of about 15 chainable input scanners and 20 chainable output scanners that sit in front of and behind an LLM call to sanitize, detect, and block unsafe or sensitive content.
reports.core_functionality: LLM Guard (package llm_guard, folders llm_guard/input_scanners and llm_guard/output_scanners) defines a common Scanner interface where each scanner's scan() method returns the possibly-modified text, a pass/fail boolean, and a 0-1 risk score. Scanners run in a list/pipeline before the prompt is sent to the LLM and again after the response comes back. Under the hood it is a hybrid: some scanners are pure library/regex logic (BanSubstrings, Regex, Secrets via bc-detect-secrets, TokenLimit via tiktoken), the PII scanner wraps Microsoft Presidio (presidio-analyzer/anonymizer) plus a Hugging Face DeBERTa NER model (ai4privacy) and stores redacted values in a Vault object so an output-side Deanonymize scanner can restore them, and several scanners load ProtectAI's own fine-tuned DeBERTa-v3 classifier models from Hugging Face for prompt-injection detection, zero-shot topic classification, toxicity, bias, and a cross-encoder NLI model for FactualConsistency (entailment scoring between context and output) and Relevance.

Flags sensitive entities appearing in the model's output specifically.

Detect programming-language code blocks in input or output to block code-injection or unwanted code generation/execution paths.
Detects invisible/zero-width Unicode characters sometimes used to smuggle hidden instructions past filters.
Checks URLs in output against malicious-URL heuristics and reachability to catch phishing or dead/attacker-controlled links.
Generic custom regex allow/deny-list scanner usable for any bespoke pattern (region-specific ID formats, banned strings, etc.).
Uses a zero-shot DeBERTa classifier to block configurable restricted topics without retraining.
Deterministic block-list/deny-list of exact strings or phrases.
Hugging Face toxicity classifier scores input/output for toxic language.
Flags overly negative or hostile tone in prompt or response.
Business-policy filter that blocks mentions of named competitor products/brands, a brand-governance control rather than a safety one.
Enforces a maximum token budget per prompt to control cost and prevent context-stuffing abuse.
Estimates and caps response reading time as a UX/SLA guard.
Model-based classifier flags nonsensical or garbled text on either side of the conversation.
Cross-encoder NLI model scores entailment between source/prompt and the LLM's output; low entailment score flags a likely hallucination.
Checks whether the output is actually on-topic relative to the prompt.
Flags when the model refused to answer, useful for catching over-refusal/availability regressions.
Validates that structured output is well-formed JSON, using json-repair to attempt automatic fixes.
Confirms output language matches the expected/input language, catching off-target-language regressions.
Model-based classifier scores output text for biased language.

limitations: Project is explicitly marked ARCHIVED by Protect AI in the README banner - no longer actively developed or maintained, so new attack patterns and CVEs will not get first-party fixes.
Most accuracy comes from specific pinned Hugging Face model revisions; model quality can drift or become stale as new jailbreak styles emerge and will not be retrained by the maintainers.
Model-based scanners need torch and transformers (heavy dependencies) and benefit strongly from a GPU or ONNX runtime for latency; CPU-only production use can be slow at scale.
One gated model requires Hugging Face approval/token, adding friction.

Default thresholds (0.92 injection, 0.75 entailment, 0.5 anonymize) are tuned on the maintainers' own benchmarks and will likely need re-tuning on AFNI's real traffic to control false positive and negative rates.
No production support channel any more given archived status; community Slack/GitHub issues are the only fallback.
